nodes.title: SG-5.5 Phaser scene is a thin wrapper over the generic scene builder
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene (game/frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts) preloads assets and builds effects, but it never calls buildScene, and no Phaser-backed RenderContext exists. Desired behavior: BootScene delegates object creation to the engine's buildScene using a Phaser RenderContext and the bundled bedroom scene content. Expected result: every object on screen comes from content, and BootScene names no object id or asset id. Why: future AI cycles must add or replace objects by editing content only.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the bundled bedroom scene, when BootScene.create runs, then buildScene is called once with that scene and a Phaser-backed RenderContext
- Given BootScene.ts and the Phaser render context source, when scanned, then neither contains a bedroom object id or asset id literal
- Given a shared-store state change, when it fires, then every built SceneObject receives sync(state)
- Given BootScene shutdown, when it fires, then every SceneObject is destroyed and the store subscription is removed


## Scope
- In scope: Phaser RenderContext implementation
- In scope: BootScene wiring of buildScene, state sync and cleanup
- In scope: Forwarding object clicks to the typed phaserToReact bus
- Out of scope: New assets or new scene content
- Out of scope: Character animation
- Out of scope: React UI changes
- Out of scope: Backend changes
- Preserve: Existing preload, fallback texture and effects wiring in BootScene
- Preserve: Existing buildScene, SceneObject and layerDepth behavior
- Preserve: Typed event bus contract in events.ts


## Technical constraints
- Phaser 3.90 APIs only
- Engine modules under game/src/engine must not import Phaser
- Game state stays in the Zustand store, BootScene keeps no copy


## Definition of done
- All acceptance criteria are met
- BootScene contains no hardcoded object
- Existing BootScene tests still pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Pixel-art friendly rendering: no smoothing on sprites


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · A Phaser-backed RenderContext draws sprites from engine specs
nodes.body:
Context: RenderContext and RenderHandle exist in game/src/engine/renderContext.ts, but only EffectRenderContext has a Phaser implementation (effectContext.ts). Desired behavior: a Phaser implementation creates an image per RenderSpriteSpec at its position, scale and depth, with hover highlight, a name label, visibility, hit bounds and click. Expected result: SceneObject can render in Phaser. Why: it is the only missing piece between buildScene and the canvas.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a RenderSpriteSpec, when createSprite runs, then an image is added with key resolved through resolveKey, the spec x, y, scale and depth
- Given spec.bounds, when createSprite runs, then the image is made interactive with a hit rectangle equal to the bounds
- Given a handle, when setHighlighted(true) and setLabelVisible(true) are called, then a tint is applied and the label text is shown, and both are cleared on false
- Given a handle, when destroy runs, then the image and the label are destroyed


## Scope
- In scope: New frontend/src/phaser/renderContext.ts
- Out of scope: Effects context changes
- Out of scope: Character sprites
- Preserve: effectContext.ts behavior
- Preserve: RenderContext interface


## Technical constraints
- Phaser 3.90 APIs only
- Resolve texture keys through an injected resolveKey function so the fallback texture applies


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- createPhaserRenderContext is exported and implements RenderContext


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · BootScene builds its objects from content via buildScene with none hardcoded
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.create only builds effects. runtime/content.ts exports scene as an unvalidated SceneDef, while buildScene needs a SceneSpec. Desired behavior: content.ts also exports a schema-validated sceneSpec, and BootScene.create builds the objects with buildScene(createPhaserRenderContext(...), sceneSpec). Expected result: all objects come from bedroom.yaml. Why: the scene is content-driven.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the bundled scene, when create runs, then buildScene is called once with sceneSpec and a context exposing createSprite
- Given BootScene.ts and renderContext.ts, when read as text, then no object id (bed, bookshelf, etc.) or asset id literal appears
- Given shutdown, when the SHUTDOWN callback runs, then destroy is called on every built SceneObject


## Scope
- In scope: content.ts sceneSpec export
- In scope: BootScene.create and shutdown wiring
- Out of scope: Changing bedroom.yaml
- Out of scope: State sync
- Preserve: scene export
- Preserve: effects and transition wiring
- Preserve: FALLBACK_KEY export


## Technical constraints
- Use sceneSchema from game/src/content/schema.ts for validation


## Dependencies
- R1


## Definition of done
- BootScene builds objects via buildScene only


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · BootScene syncs objects with the store and forwards clicks to React
nodes.body:
Context: SceneObject.sync applies visibleWhen and onInteract reports activations; BootScene.onStateChange currently only reads state. Desired behavior: after building, BootScene syncs every object with the current state and on each store change, and emits phaserToReact objectClick with the object id on activation. Expected result: persistent object state (e.g. secret door) shows after changes. Why: React and Phaser stay consistent without duplicate state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a non-null store state, when create runs, then sync(state) is called on each built object
- Given a store change to a new state, when onStateChange runs, then sync(newState) is called on each object
- Given a null state, when onStateChange runs, then no sync is called
- Given an object's onInteract callback, when invoked with objectId, then phaserToReact.emit('objectClick', {id}) is called


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.create, onStateChange
- Out of scope: Hover events
- Out of scope: Keyboard focus wiring
- Preserve: readState
- Preserve: subscription cleanup


## Technical constraints
- No GameState copy kept in BootScene


## Dependencies
- R2


## Definition of done
- Objects reflect store state and clicks reach the bus


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.description: Create game/frontend/src/phaser/renderContext.ts exporting createPhaserRenderContext(scene, resolveKey) that returns a RenderContext whose createSprite builds a Phaser image, label text and RenderHandle.
acceptance_criteria: createSprite places an image using the spec position, scale, depth and resolved key
The handle implements highlight, label, visibility, hover, click and destroy

steps.action: Create the file importing Phaser, RenderContext, RenderHandle and RenderSpriteSpec from '@game/engine/renderContext'. Export createPhaserRenderContext(scene: Phaser.Scene, resolveKey: (id: string) => string): RenderContext whose createSprite(spec) does: image = scene.add.image(spec.x, spec.y, resolveKey(spec.key)).setOrigin(0,0).setScale(spec.scale).setDepth(spec.depth); if spec.bounds, image.setInteractive(new Phaser.Geom.Rectangle(b.x,b.y,b.width,b.height), Phaser.Geom.Rectangle.Contains); label = scene.add.text(spec.x, spec.y - 12, spec.label ?? '', {fontSize:'10px'}).setDepth(spec.depth+0.5).setVisible(false).
steps.code: export function createPhaserRenderContext(scene: Phaser.Scene, resolveKey: (id: string) => string): RenderContext { return { createSprite(spec) { /* as described */ } }; }
steps.expected: Function exported and returns an object with createSprite

steps.action: Return a RenderHandle: setVisible(v) calls image.setVisible(v) and, when v is false, label.setVisible(false); setHighlighted(on) calls image.setTint(0xfff2b0) when on else image.clearTint(); setLabelVisible(on) calls label.setVisible(on); onHover(cb) registers image.on('pointerover', () => cb(true)) and image.on('pointerout', () => cb(false)); onClick(cb) registers image.on('pointerdown', cb); destroy() calls image.destroy() and label.destroy().
steps.expected: All six RenderHandle methods exist and delegate to Phaser objects
